adult.note: Modern practice: 0.5–0.75 mg per 100 U heparin is often sufficient (Mondal 2024) — over-dosing risks paradoxical anticoagulation, platelet dysfunction, and increased reaction risk. Titrate by HMS-Hepcon or post-protamine ACT. Single-dose cap 50 mg.

riskFactors: Fish allergy (true cross-reactivity is uncommon but increased risk)
Prior exposure to protamine (especially repeat cardiac surgery, repeat catheterisation)
NPH insulin / protamine-containing insulin users (~15-fold increased risk of IgE-mediated reaction)
History of vasectomy (sperm-protamine antibodies — disputed but cited)
preventionStrategy: Slow administration: ≥ 10 min for full dose; first 5–10 mg as test dose over 1–2 min then pause
Adequate volume + euvolaemia before administration (hypovolaemic patients more prone to hypotension)
Have noradrenaline / phenylephrine drawn up and primed before starting
Have heparin available — reheparinisation + return to CPB is the rescue option for catastrophic Type III
TOE in place — early warning of RV dilatation in Type III pulmonary vasoconstriction
High-risk patients: pre-treat with H1+H2 blockers + steroids; consider heparinase as alternative or omit reversal in OPCAB / endovascular cases

reactionTypes.typeI: Type I — systemic hypotension (most common, ~3-6%). Rate-related vasodilation + histamine release. Pause infusion; fluid + phenylephrine; restart at slower rate.
reactionTypes.typeII: Type II — anaphylactic/anaphylactoid (IgE or complement-mediated). Hypotension + bronchospasm + flushing ± urticaria. Stop protamine; treat as anaphylaxis (adrenaline IM/IV, fluids, steroids per UK Resus 2025 if biphasic concern). Mast cell tryptase × 3.
reactionTypes.typeIII: Type III — catastrophic pulmonary vasoconstriction (rare, ~0.2%, mortality 25–30%). Acute pulmonary HTN, RV failure, systemic collapse. STOP protamine. Reheparinise (full dose 300 U/kg). Return to CPB if possible. iNO 20–40 ppm or inhaled prostacyclin. Inotrope (milrinone, dobutamine) for RV failure. ECMO if refractory.

cautions: Hypotension with rapid infusion (slow IV over ≥ 10 min mandatory)
Pulmonary hypertension
Anaphylaxis (Type II) — especially fish allergy, NPH insulin, prior exposure
Catastrophic pulmonary vasoconstriction (Type III) — heparinise + return to CPB
